title: Recipe repo sync
lead: Clone, pull, commit and push the household's recipe repo (`recipe_repo_url`) using a repo-scoped deploy key (ADR 0012).
boundary: **Not in this slice:** the importer; any admin UI for conflicts (this slice only exposes `status()`; the page is S66); the scheduler itself (S64).

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: Recipes live in git. larder must read the latest version and push its own changes without ever needing broader credentials. The git host is whatever `recipe_repo_url` names; any host that accepts a deploy key works (ADR 0012).

sections.heading: Owner input
sections.body:
Owner checklist (the owner does these on their git host; no agent runs host tooling or touches the host):
1. Create an empty repo on your git host and set `recipe_repo_url` (in `larder.toml` or `LARDER_RECIPE_REPO_URL`).
2. Generate a deploy key with write access and add its public half to that repo in the host's settings. Put the private key at `$LARDER_DATA/secrets/deploy_key` (or the `[secrets] deploy_key` path), mode 0600. It is never committed.
3. Add the host's SSH key to `$LARDER_DATA/secrets/known_hosts` so ssh never prompts.

Decisions:
4. Sync cadence: on startup, every N minutes (recommend 15) and after each write?
5. On divergence: rebase local commits onto the remote (recommended), or stop and show "needs attention"?

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `src/larder/recipes/repo.py`
- `src/larder/web/__init__.py` (`create_app` registers the sync job on S64's scheduler when `recipe_repo_url` is set)
- `tests/test_recipe_repo.py` (uses a local bare repo as the "remote")

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
1. `test_clone_when_missing_then_pull_when_present`
2. `test_commit_and_push_writes_file_with_configured_identity`
3. `test_push_uses_deploy_key_via_GIT_SSH_COMMAND_only`
4. `test_diverged_remote_rebases_cleanly`
5. `test_conflict_surfaces_status_and_leaves_repo_clean`
6. `test_secrets_never_logged`
7. `test_status_before_first_clone_and_when_in_sync`
8. `test_conflict_status_is_readable_from_a_new_process`
9. `test_sync_job_is_registered_only_when_the_repo_url_is_set` (run it with `Scheduler.run_due()` and an injected clock)
10. `test_git_calls_are_serialized_by_the_lock_file`

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Wrap git via `subprocess.run([...], check=True)` with no shell. Set `GIT_SSH_COMMAND` to `ssh -i <key> -o IdentitiesOnly=yes -o BatchMode=yes -o UserKnownHostsFile=<known_hosts> -o StrictHostKeyChecking=yes`.
2. Functions take `settings` first: `ensure_clone(settings)`, `pull(settings)`, `commit(settings, paths, message)`, `push(settings)`, `status(settings) -> RepoStatus`. `RepoStatus` is a frozen dataclass: `state` (`not_cloned`, `ok` or `needs_attention`), `detail`, `last_sync_at`, `ahead`, `behind`, `conflicted_files`. S66 renders it.
3. Divergence policy per Owner input; abort the rebase on conflict and write the status to `.git/larder-status.json` inside the clone (never committed), so a later process can read it.
4. Take an exclusive `fcntl.flock` on `$LARDER_DATA/recipes.lock` around git operations so the scheduler and requests don't race.
5. Log commands without secrets.
6. `register_sync(scheduler, settings, interval_seconds=900)` registers a "recipe-sync" job on the scheduler S64 provides that calls `pull`. S13 adds the index hook later.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
- Repo tests pass against a local bare repo.
- With the owner: the owner checklist is done, the real repo clones, and a test commit pushes (then is reverted only if the owner asks).

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: Commit only when the owner asks; no AI attribution.
